summary: Le Havre is a dense Uwe Rosenberg resource-conversion game where you shuffle raw goods through a chain of buildings to turn wood and clay into food, iron, steel, and eventually ships and victory points. It's a slow, cerebral engine-builder where every turn is an agonizing choice between feeding your workers and investing in long-term infrastructure.
praised: building ownership creates passive income streams
criticised: long playtime, especially at higher player counts
heavy analysis paralysis due to many building options
steep learning curve for new players
can feel like a solitaire game with others at the table

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with some building-fee taxation
interaction.detail: Players mainly develop their own tableau of buildings and resources, but the shared offer spaces and the fact that you pay rivals when using buildings they own not you creates light indirect interaction. Turn order and taking whole offer stacks before opponents can also matter tactically.

scoring.why: Final ranking is total franc value: cash on hand plus the sale value of all remaining goods, buildings, and ships.
scoring.how_you_win: Build up a portfolio of buildings, ships, and stockpiled goods while keeping enough food to avoid penalties; at game end everything you own is converted to its money value and the richest player wins.
